physics_goals.quote: The primary goal of the SoLid experiment is to perform a precise measurement of the electron antineutrino energy spectrum and flux and to search for very short distance neutrino oscillations as a probe of eV-scale sterile neutrinos.
physics_goals.value: Measure the electron-antineutrino energy spectrum and flux very close to a research-reactor core and search for very-short-distance oscillations as a probe of eV-scale sterile neutrinos

summary.plain: A detector built from thousands of small plastic-scintillator cubes, placed just metres from the compact core of the BR2 research reactor in Belgium, to look for sterile neutrinos. It collected data from 2018 to 2020 and has published constraints on the reactor antineutrino anomaly.
summary.technical: Search for Oscillations with a Lithium-6 detector: 12,800 voxels (PVT cubes with 6LiF:ZnS(Ag) screens, MPPC readout, 3D imaging) in a shipping container at 6.3-8.9 m from the BR2 core (40-100 MW_th, 93.5 % 235U) under ~8 m.w.e. Data April 2018 - July 2020: 280 reactor-on and 172 reactor-off days, 29,479 antineutrino candidates; model-dependent fits constrain the RAA allowed region.
